Nema for Procurement

Know what renews and who must decide.

Nema organizes vendor records and contract facts into a reviewable queue for procurement. Buyers and business owners retain negotiation, legal interpretation, approval, and purchasing authority.

All teams ↗

Turn a contract into a decision schedule

Renewals are easy to miss when the agreement, notice period, owner, usage context, and prior decision live in different places. Nema can prepare a renewal packet from the signed document and approved vendor records.

Ask for exact page citations on renewal, notice, term, and pricing facts. Supply the team's lead-time rule so reminder dates come from an explicit calculation. Procurement verifies every material term before relying on the schedule.

Complete vendor intake

Give Nema the intake policy and required fields for a new vendor. It can identify missing business owner, use case, users, data access, budget, alternatives, security review, and commercial documents. The requester receives a clear list instead of several rounds of follow-up.

The output can propose the next review step and its owner. Procurement decides whether the request is complete, which assessments apply, and whether the company should proceed.

Compare quotes on agreed criteria

Provide the quotes, common scope, volume assumptions, and evaluation criteria. Nema can normalize named line items, show exclusions, and produce a comparison table with source citations.

It should not treat unlike bundles as directly comparable or select a winner. The buyer checks taxes, terms, service levels, implementation, and total commercial context before making a recommendation.

Answer purchasing-policy questions

Nema can retrieve the current purchasing policy and explain required thresholds, documentation, and approval routes. A cited answer helps requesters prepare the right packet before procurement reviews it.

Exceptions and ambiguous categories go to the policy owner. The workflow helps people follow the process; it does not approve spend or interpret contract law.

Run an exception-led renewal review

A recurring report can show agreements entering their review window, records with no owner, and packets missing usage or commercial inputs. Keep the source date visible and limit the audience to people allowed to see the vendor terms.

Once the business owner chooses renew, renegotiate, or exit, Nema can draft the follow-up tasks. Procurement and legal owners review any external message or system change.

Start with one agreement

Choose a sample contract with a clear renewal term and one ambiguous clause. Verify the extracted facts and page citations. The ambiguity should route to the contract owner rather than disappear into a calculated date.

After the review, Nema can turn the stated decision into a short follow-up plan. A renewal may need a negotiation owner, a usage check, and a legal review date. An exit may need notice preparation and a replacement plan. Each task remains tied to the source decision.

The same structure works for quarterly vendor reviews. Instead of rereading every agreement, the team can focus on renewals entering the decision window, suppliers with unresolved service issues, and packets still missing required information.

Questions from procurement teams

Can Nema read contracts and PDFs?

It can work with authorized files and cite pages. Procurement or legal reviewers should confirm dates, scope, and meaning in the original agreement.

Does Nema negotiate or approve purchases?

No. Nema prepares review material. Authorized people negotiate, interpret terms, approve spend, and commit the company.

Can Nema compare quotes?

Yes, when you provide common assumptions and criteria. It should expose exclusions and differences instead of reducing the decision to one price.
